newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Cardenas sees sharp fall in stocks.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Cardenas sees sharp fall in stocks.

text.p: The head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said he sees the country's coffee stocks falling to 3.5 million 60-kg bags by September from six million held in inventory during the same month a year ago.
"Inventories could drop to 3.5 million bags by the end of September 1997," Cardenas told reporters.

Earlier this month, Cardenas said inventories stood at about five million 60-kg bags, indicating that the federation plans to draw heavily on existing stockpiles to fulfill Colombia's export commitments between now and September.
Cardenas, who spoke at an impromptu news conference after a weekly federation policy meeting, did not elaborate on the issue of Colombian stocks or how much of them consisted of old crop coffee.

But he said Colombia was looking at coffee output during the current coffee year of no more than about 10 million bags, slightly lower than previous estimates and well below the 13 million bags produced during the 1995/96 coffee year.

He also said expectations of a smaller-than-average 1997/98 crop in Brazil should be constructive in terms of near-term market prices but declined to be more specific, other than to say that industry sources were talking about a Brazilian crop of no more than 23 million bags.
